name: Fujian Tulou
description: In the hills of south-west Fujian, 46 huge earthen houses rise from fields of rice, tea and tobacco. Built between the 15th and 20th centuries, these round or square fortresses have thick mud walls and a single gate. Each sheltered a whole clan, up to 800 people, around an open courtyard. Behind their plain exteriors, the homes inside are often richly decorated.
